statement: Prove that the product of the first $n$ natural numbers is divisible by the sum of the first $n$ natural numbers if and only if $n + 1$ is not an odd prime.

For $x, y, z \geq 0$, establish the inequality
$$x(x-z)^2 + y(y-z)^2 \geq (x-z)(y-z)(x+y-z)$$
and determine when equality holds.

$ABCD$ is a square with $U$ and $V$ interior points of sides $AB$ and $CD$ respectively. $P$ and $Q$ are the intersections of $UV$ with the diagonals of the square. Determine all ways of selecting $U$ and $V$ so as to maximize the area of quadrilateral $PUQV$.
figure_description: Square ABCD with interior points U on AB and V on CD; line UV intersects the two diagonals at points P and Q, forming quadrilateral PUQV.

statement: A deck of $2n+1$ cards consists of a joker and, for each number between $1$ and $n$ inclusive, two cards marked with that number. The $2n+1$ cards are placed in a row with the joker in the middle. For each $k$ with $1 \leq k \leq n$, the two cards numbered $k$ have exactly $k-1$ cards between them. Determine all values of $n$ not exceeding $10$ for which this arrangement is possible. For which values of $n$ is it impossible?
